/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:7264:{"content":"## The one fact that determines the whole architecture\n\nThe user runs aimee-server; the organization runs aimee-kb. From the org's point of view aimee-server is therefore an untrusted process — the user controls its memory, its env, its disk. Two consequences follow, and they are not optional:\n\n1. **Org vendor keys must never reach aimee-server.** A key placed in a user-controlled process is a key handed to the user. Therefore aimee-kb — not the server — must be the **egress authority** for org models: server → kb → vendor. The server sees prompts and completions, never an org key.\n2. **Identity is federated, not key-shaped.** Machines/servers always authenticate with enrollment certs (`cert:CN`); when the org configures it on kb, users additionally authenticate with OIDC (the org IdP). aimee-kb therefore always knows who is calling — which is exactly what a \"virtual key\" would otherwise be inventing.\n\n**OIDC is optional — never required unless configured on aimee-kb.** It layers on additively (exactly as the existing verifier does — opt-in via `AIMEE_KB_OIDC_JWKS_FILE`, registered after the owner token). The always-present identity is the enrollment cert; when no OIDC is configured, team binding and attribution key off `cert:CN` and the existing owner-token/bearer auth, and nothing in the series stops working. A single-org box with no IdP still runs the whole plan on certs alone.","doc_id":"470ee1ed8cddddbf8df51c8e","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:7680:{"content":"## What already exists (why this is wiring, not green-field)\n\nThe four-way code survey (2026-07-17) found aimee already owns most of the hard primitives the commercial tools charge enterprise money for:\n\n- **Cost accounting — strong.** Per-request token→USD in the `token_audit` DB1 table (`src/db1/token_audit.c`, `src/server/token_tracker.c`): multi-source pricing (static table → registry/models.dev → authoritative DB1 `model_pricing`), attributed by model/source/role/tool/session/principal/delegation with parent cost-fold. Read surface exists: `GET /v1/insights/overview`, `/v1/dashboard/*`, React `CostPanel`. **Missing only the per-team/project dimension.**\n- **Credential vault — encrypted at rest**, keyed by attested principal (`src/server/vault_service.c`, `src/headers/vault_principal.h`).\n- **OIDC/JWT verifier — real** (RS256/JWKS, alg-pinned), in aimee-kb and kb-console (`src/kb/auth_oidc.c`, `kb-console/auth.go`) — opt-in via env today.\n- **PKI + mTLS enrollment CA** (`src/kb/enroll.c`, `src/kb/pki.c`, `src/server/kb_client_mtls.c`) — `aimee://` single-use tokens, `cert:CN` principals. Reusable for enrolling servers.\n- **Canonical IR + provider drivers** (`src/headers/aimee_ir.h`, `src/server/delegate_driver.c`, `aimee-universal-gateway.md`, done) — Anthropic / OpenAI-Chat / Responses / Gemini wire adapters through a protocol-neutral pivot. This is the egress machinery kb needs.\n- **Keyless roster + attested credential handling already exist** — the shipped `deploy/container/agents.json` ships no keys. The old client-push `POST /v1/session/credentials` was retired; provider secrets now live in the server vault (`/v1/vault/*`), and vault writes require an attested transport (UDS or confidential TLS+bearer — never plaintext TCP; `server_cert.c:18-22`, `server_http_identity.c:113-123`). The org-egress work reuses this attested-transport discipline rather than inventing a new one — org keys simply never leave kb in the first place.\n\nAbsent (the actual gaps, one sub-proposal each): a team/project entity; per-team/project cost attribution; per-team budgets and per-key rate limits (spend is tracked but never capped; the rate limiter is a single global bucket); OIDC on the aimee-server data plane + a kb→server control plane; and AWS Bedrock.","doc_id":"4ae8738e9a2b00bd4911be43","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:9271:{"content":"## Exact token contract\n\nAdd a bounded `server_mgmt_token_claims_t` populated by one parser/verifier pass. The compact JWT\nhas exactly three nonempty canonical base64url segments, no padding, no whitespace, and bounds of\n1024 header bytes, 4096 payload bytes, 512 signature bytes, and 8192 wire bytes. Decode and\nre-encode each segment byte-for-byte before use. Reject\nembedded NUL, invalid trailing bits, overflow, duplicate JSON member names at any level, unknown\nmembers, wrong types, non-integer numbers, and values outside their destination buffers.\n\nThe protected header contains exactly `alg`, `typ`, and `kid`: `alg` is exactly `RS256`, `typ` is\nexactly `JWT`, and `kid` is a nonempty 1..64-byte ASCII token. No `crit`, `jku`, `x5u`, embedded JWK, or\nalgorithm/key-type fallback is accepted. Select exactly one RSA public key from the caller-supplied\nauthenticated JWKS by exact `kid`; duplicate kids, unknown fields relevant to key interpretation,\nwrong kty/use/alg, malformed modulus/exponent, weak keys, or multiple matches fail closed. Accept\nRSA moduli from 2048 through 8192 bits only and an odd exponent from 3 through `INT32_MAX`; verify\nwith explicit SHA-256 and RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 padding rather than relying on the JOSE header alone.\nThe supplied JWKS blob is a pure verifier input whose authenticity is a precondition in C1a tests;\nauthenticated fetch, signed generation/HWM, refresh, and rotation are owned by P5-C2.\n\nThe payload contains exactly these typed claims:\n\n- `v`: integer `1`;\n- `iss`: exact configured kb management issuer;\n- `aud`: exact target `AIMEE_SERVER_ID`, as one string rather than an array;\n- `sub`: at most 576 bytes and exactly the P1 `kb_identity_key` form: `owner`,\n  `oidc:<percent-encoded-issuer>:<percent-encoded-subject>`, or\n  `cert:<percent-encoded-issuer>:<normalized-serial>`; percent escapes are uppercase and only\n  `%25`/`%3A`, components are nonempty and control-free, and a bare OIDC subject is invalid;\n- `team_id`: a positive signed 64-bit tenant id bound by the kb authorization decision;","doc_id":"5a499b2160a08e67c81d44e6","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:9733:{"content":"## §3 OIDC on the kb data plane — additive and optional\n\nPromote the existing verifier to a first-class, documented data-plane\nauthenticator: when configured, a request bearing a valid OIDC JWT is\nauthenticated as the issuer-scoped identity `(iss, sub)` (never a bare `user:<sub>`) and resolved via §2.\n\n**OIDC is never required — it is enabled only when the org configures it on kb**\n(the verifier already registers *additively* after the owner token, opt-in via\n`AIMEE_KB_OIDC_JWKS_FILE`). When OIDC is not configured:\n- `cert:CN` (enrollment) is the always-present identity, and §2 binds teams off it.\n- Human callers use the existing owner-token/bearer auth; team binding can map a\n  configured owner/bearer to a default team.\n- Nothing in §1–§4 (or in P2–P5) depends on OIDC being present. OIDC only *adds*\n  a human-SSO identity source. A single-org box with no IdP runs entirely on\n  certs.\n\n**Revocation caveat.** OIDC JWTs are bearer tokens valid until their `exp`; the\nverifier is stateless (signature + `exp`, no introspection or revocation lookup —\n`auth_oidc.c`), so IdP-side revocation of a leaked token takes effect only at\nexpiry. A deployment that needs fast human-credential revocation must set short IdP\naccess-token lifetimes (≤15 min recommended); the machine spine stays real-time\nvia `cert.revoke`, enforced per request (not only at the mTLS handshake — see §2).\nkb additionally enforces a **hard server-side ceiling on accepted token age** —\n`now − iat ≤ configured max` (default 15 min) — rejecting an over-age token with a\ntyped error **regardless of the token's own `exp`**, so a leaked or misconfigured\nlong-lived token cannot outlive the ceiling even if the IdP sets a longer expiry. The\ncheck is not bypassable by a bad `iat`: kb **requires a numeric `iat`, rejects a missing\nor malformed one, rejects an `iat` in the future beyond a small clock-skew allowance,\nand computes age with overflow-safe arithmetic** — critically, it **rejects `now < iat`","doc_id":"5ec94ad4b0979a5b53377c3c","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:10170:{"content":"## Helper trust and file boundary\n\nThe configured helper and every ancestor must be root-owned, regular/directory as\nappropriate, non-symlink, and not group/world writable. Resolve every absolute-path\ncomponent with `openat(O_NOFOLLOW)` from an opened `/`, verify each descriptor with\n`fstat`, and execute the checked leaf descriptor with Linux\n`execveat(AT_EMPTY_PATH)` rather than reopening a path. B2a accepts a native ELF\nhelper only, avoiding the CLOEXEC interpreter-script ambiguity. Refuse setuid/setgid\nfiles. Unsupported platforms return DISABLED. The parent creates CLOEXEC pipes,\nforks with a precomputed fd bound, and the child receives only stdin/stdout; stderr\nand every unrelated fd are closed. Before descriptor exec the child sets\n`PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`; the environment is an explicit empty array. A five-second\nabsolute deadline covers request write, response read, and normal child exit. On\nexpiry the parent kills the helper process group and exactly reaps the direct child;\nthe final kernel reap can extend past the deadline only for an uninterruptible task,\navoiding zombies at the cost of that explicit kernel-state exception. Calls on one\nprovider are mutex-serialized so a provider cannot create an unbounded concurrent\nchild set.\nShort/extra output, signal exit, timeout, partial framing, or diagnostics are generic\nunavailable and all request/response buffers are cleansed.\n\nThe helper is a trusted platform adapter, but its assertions are not trusted\nwithout independent cryptographic verification: C verifies the workload JWT under\nthe pinned JWKS and verifies a response-binding ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 signature under\nthe pinned proof SPKI. Its SHA-256 is `proof_anchor_id`; a distinct\n`custody_anchor_id` is SHA-256 of the provider wrapping-key resource identifier and\nis included in every proof. Deployment must policy-bind that proof key and\nwrap/unwrap permission to the same platform principal. The C boundary proves the\nJWT, the pinned-helper proof, and the exact transcript; it cannot prove cloud IAM","doc_id":"631aacc2ecdb2c876db464c8","doc_kind":""}

Static (compile-time) — no DB/reload\n  dependency; updating the table is a deployment-time change, documented.\n- **Enrollment store** — `src/kb/enroll.c` (+ `kb_enroll.h`): tokens 256-bit, **only\n  `sha256(token)` persisted**; CA + CSR issuance present; **no list/revoke and no redeemed-cert\n  record today.** S2a adds the persisted row + migration (below).\n- **mTLS vs bearer are separate seams** — client-cert validation is at the TLS layer\n  (`kb_tls_serve.c`, `kb_tls.c`), NOT through `kb_verifier.h` (the OIDC/JWT/scoped-bearer seam,\n  `auth_oidc.c`). Revocation is enforced in **both**.\n- **OIDC verifier config** — `auth_oidc.c` loads JWKS/iss/aud/claim-map. S2b makes it\n  DB2-backed (`kb_oidc_config`) behind `GET/PUT /v1/config/oidc`, live-applied via\n  [[live-config-reload-initiative]] (merged #1056).\n- **Governance data** — `decision_log` (`schema.sql:49`; one-active-per-scope\n  `idx_dl_active_scope` — a partial UNIQUE index `WHERE status='active'`) + `audit_events`\n  (`schema.sql:526`); DB2 API + `kb_client_*` wrappers exist.\n- **Dashboard telemetry (served)** — `/v1/ingest/status`, `/v1/corpus/pipeline/status`,","doc_id":"69967d312d1713a054074c14","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:10848:{"content":"## Exact token contract\n\nAdd a bounded `server_mgmt_token_claims_t` populated by one parser/verifier pass. The compact JWT\nhas exactly three nonempty canonical base64url segments, no padding, no whitespace, and bounds of\n1024 header bytes, 4096 payload bytes, 512 signature bytes, and 8192 wire bytes. Decode and\nre-encode each segment byte-for-byte before use. Reject\nembedded NUL, invalid trailing bits, overflow, duplicate JSON member names at any level, unknown\nmembers, wrong types, non-integer numbers, and values outside their destination buffers.\n\nThe protected header contains exactly `alg`, `typ`, and `kid`: `alg` is exactly `RS256`, `typ` is\nexactly `JWT`, and `kid` is a nonempty 1..64-byte ASCII token. No `crit`, `jku`, `x5u`, embedded JWK, or\nalgorithm/key-type fallback is accepted. Select exactly one RSA public key from the caller-supplied\nauthenticated JWKS by exact `kid`; duplicate kids, unknown fields relevant to key interpretation,\nwrong kty/use/alg, malformed modulus/exponent, weak keys, or multiple matches fail closed. Accept\nRSA moduli from 2048 through 8192 bits only and an odd exponent from 3 through `INT32_MAX`; verify\nwith explicit SHA-256 and RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 padding rather than relying on the JOSE header alone.\nThe supplied JWKS blob is a pure verifier input whose authenticity is a precondition in C1a tests;\nauthenticated fetch, signed generation/HWM, refresh, and rotation are owned by P5-C2.\n\nThe payload contains exactly these typed claims:\n\n- `v`: integer `1`;\n- `iss`: exact configured kb management issuer;\n- `aud`: exact target `AIMEE_SERVER_ID`, as one string rather than an array;\n- `sub`: at most 576 bytes and exactly the P1 `kb_identity_key` form: `owner`,\n  `oidc:<percent-encoded-issuer>:<percent-encoded-subject>`, or\n  `cert:<percent-encoded-issuer>:<normalized-serial>`; percent escapes are uppercase and only\n  `%25`/`%3A`, components are nonempty and control-free, and a bare OIDC subject is invalid;\n- `team_id`: a positive signed 64-bit tenant id bound by the kb authorization decision;","doc_id":"69a94fb2f7fe718fa88da3e8","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:11144:{"content":"func (j *jwksCache) key(kid string) (*rsa.PublicKey, error) {\n\tj.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer j.mu.Unlock()\n\tif k, ok := j.keys[kid]; ok && time.Since(j.fetched) < j.ttl {\n\t\treturn k, nil\n\t}\n\tif err := j.refresh(); err != nil {\n\t\tif k, ok := j.keys[kid]; ok && time.Since(j.fetched) < j.maxStale {\n\t\t\treturn k, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tk, ok := j.keys[kid]\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"no JWKS key for kid %q\", kid)\n\t}\n\treturn k, nil\n}\n\nfunc (j *jwksCache) refresh() error {\n\t// HTTPS-only, no redirects, bounded body — the basic SSRF/rebind defenses.\n\t// S2b adds the full private-range denial + DNS-rebind re-check when the URL\n\t// becomes operator-editable via /v1/config/oidc.\n\tif u, err := url.Parse(j.url); err != nil || u.Scheme != \"https\" || u.Host == \"\" {\n\t\treturn errors.New(\"jwks url must be an absolute https URL\")\n\t}\n\tclient := j.client\n\tif client == nil {\n\t\tclient = &http.Client{\n\t\t\tTimeout: 5 * time.Second,\n\t\t\tCheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error {\n\t\t\t\treturn errors.New(\"jwks: redirects not allowed\")\n\t\t\t},\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tresp, err := client.Get(j.url)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tdefer resp.Body.Close()\n\tif resp.StatusCode != 200 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"jwks fetch: status %d\", resp.StatusCode)\n\t}\n\tvar doc struct {\n\t\tKeys []struct {\n\t\t\tKid string `json:\"kid\"`\n\t\t\tKty string `json:\"kty\"`\n\t\t\tN   string `json:\"n\"`\n\t\t\tE   string `json:\"e\"`\n\t\t} `json:\"keys\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := json.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20)).Decode(&doc); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tnext := map[string]*rsa.Public","doc_id":"6c845025eefc43776da7c650","doc_kind":"code_unit_body"}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:11257:{"content":"## Objective and boundary\n\nComplete the public half of the P5 management-token trust path: an enrolled aimee-server fetches the immutable C2b signed JWKS envelope from aimee-kb over the existing pinned server-to-kb mTLS channel, validates it against an independently operator-installed C2a public trust bundle, and installs it in a durable monotonic server-local cache. Add a typed unknown-`kid` verifier result and one-refresh orchestration seam for the later action composition slice.\n\nThis slice does not mint a token, use a private token key, enable `/v1/management/action`, dispatch a management mutation, or implement a generation after C2b's generation 1. If a later publisher ships generation 2, this C2c consumer continues to accept generation 1 only until a separately reviewed plan lifts the pin; it never silently gains rotation semantics. The existing unconditional action denial remains unchanged.","doc_id":"6d916ddc23e12aa58abfd6a1","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:11283:{"content":"s output copy: only\nafter the base signature/issuer/audience/time check succeeds, it decodes the\nalready-verified payload into a fresh bounded parser tree, counts and rejects\nduplicate security claims, and extracts them without truncation. It additionally\nrequires exactly one bounded nonempty printable `sub`,\ncanonical `iss`, exact audience, `iat <= now+2`, `exp > now-2`, `exp-iat <= 300`,\nrejects a present `nbf` later than now+2, and requires a remaining lifetime of at\nleast 30 seconds. Issuer and subject are each 1..600 ASCII bytes. It hashes then\ncleanses the token and every parser copy before return. Numeric dates must be finite\nexact nonnegative integers representable as `uint64_t`; arrays or fractional values\nfail.\nJWKS replacement is atomic and root-owned; each operation reads a fresh bounded\nsnapshot through a checked directory descriptor, and an unknown kid causes one\nchecked reopen/reload for that call. This ensures removal of a retired key takes\neffect without waiting for a new `kid`. \"No\nidentity cache\" means no successful token, claims, helper proof, or operation result\nis reused. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:11585:{"content":"## §3 OIDC on the kb data plane — additive and optional\n\nPromote the existing verifier to a first-class, documented data-plane\nauthenticator: when configured, a request bearing a valid OIDC JWT is\nauthenticated as the issuer-scoped identity `(iss, sub)` (never a bare `user:<sub>`) and resolved via §2.\n\n**OIDC is never required — it is enabled only when the org configures it on kb**\n(the verifier already registers *additively* after the owner token, opt-in via\n`AIMEE_KB_OIDC_JWKS_FILE`). When OIDC is not configured:\n- `cert:CN` (enrollment) is the always-present identity, and §2 binds teams off it.\n- Human callers use the existing owner-token/bearer auth; team binding can map a\n  configured owner/bearer to a default team.\n- Nothing in §1–§4 (or in P2–P5) depends on OIDC being present. OIDC only *adds*\n  a human-SSO identity source. A single-org box with no IdP runs entirely on\n  certs.\n\n**Revocation caveat.** OIDC JWTs are bearer tokens valid until their `exp`; the\nverifier is stateless (signature + `exp`, no introspection or revocation lookup —\n`auth_oidc.c`), so IdP-side revocation of a leaked token takes effect only at\nexpiry. A deployment that needs fast human-credential revocation must set short IdP\naccess-token lifetimes (≤15 min recommended); the machine spine stays real-time\nvia `cert.revoke`, enforced per request (not only at the mTLS handshake — see §2).\nkb additionally enforces a **hard server-side ceiling on accepted token age** —\n`now − iat ≤ configured max` (default 15 min) — rejecting an over-age token with a\ntyped error **regardless of the token's own `exp`**, so a leaked or misconfigured\nlong-lived token cannot outlive the ceiling even if the IdP sets a longer expiry. The\ncheck is not bypassable by a bad `iat`: kb **requires a numeric `iat`, rejects a missing\nor malformed one, rejects an `iat` in the future beyond a small clock-skew allowance,\nand computes age with overflow-safe arithmetic** — critically, it **rejects `now < iat`","doc_id":"70a79d91495de0ec0da752ce","doc_kind":""}

Today a\nshared/company KB is administered only over the CLI and raw `/v1` HTTP. The builder accepts one already-authorized immutable claim tuple and one\nnarrow RS256 signing callback. It validates and canonically serializes the tuple, asks the callback\nto sign only the resulting protected signing input, and returns a compact token in caller-owned\nbounded storage.\n\nThis packet deliberately does not generate or persist `jti`, correlation id, time, `kid`, actor,\nteam, target, peer identity, or request digest. P5-C1c owns their primary-authoritative admission\nand immutable replay tuple; P5-C2 binds the admitted `kid` to a production custody key and supplies\nthe signing callback. Keeping those values explicit makes exact retry deterministic and prevents a\nlater database authority from fighting hidden mint-side randomness or clock reads. The KB enforces the ACL\n  server-side; the Go role-gate is defence-in-depth.\n- **Revocation source of truth = DB2** (`revoked_at` on the enrollment row). The per-instance\n  in-memory check is a **read-cache** (LRU, short TTL, invalidated by a notifier from the revoke\n  write); a stale cache self-heals within the TTL, which is the documented **residual window**.\n  Multi-node coherence therefore needs no gossip — every node reads the same DB row on cache\n  miss. Single-instance is the documented default; the TTL bounds the multi-node window.\n- **Login = OIDC primary.** The Go console verifies a browser-presented OIDC JWT itself using\n  **`golang-jwt/jwt/v5`** (vendored via `go mod vendor`, committed — satisfies the no-network\n  build rule). /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:14214:{"content":"## Helper trust and file boundary\n\nThe configured helper and every ancestor must be root-owned, regular/directory as\nappropriate, non-symlink, and not group/world writable. Resolve every absolute-path\ncomponent with `openat(O_NOFOLLOW)` from an opened `/`, verify each descriptor with\n`fstat`, and execute the checked leaf descriptor with Linux\n`execveat(AT_EMPTY_PATH)` rather than reopening a path. B2a accepts a native ELF\nhelper only, avoiding the CLOEXEC interpreter-script ambiguity. Refuse setuid/setgid\nfiles. Unsupported platforms return DISABLED. The parent creates CLOEXEC pipes,\nforks with a precomputed fd bound, and the child receives only stdin/stdout; stderr\nand every unrelated fd are closed. Before descriptor exec the child sets\n`PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`; the environment is an explicit empty array. A five-second\nabsolute deadline covers request write, response read, and normal child exit. On\nexpiry the parent kills the helper process group and exactly reaps the direct child;\nthe final kernel reap can extend past the deadline only for an uninterruptible task,\navoiding zombies at the cost of that explicit kernel-state exception. Calls on one\nprovider are mutex-serialized so a provider cannot create an unbounded concurrent\nchild set.\nShort/extra output, signal exit, timeout, partial framing, or diagnostics are generic\nunavailable and all request/response buffers are cleansed.\n\nThe helper is a trusted platform adapter, but its assertions are not trusted\nwithout independent cryptographic verification: C verifies the workload JWT under\nthe pinned JWKS and verifies a response-binding ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 signature under\nthe pinned proof SPKI. Its SHA-256 is `proof_anchor_id`; a distinct\n`custody_anchor_id` is SHA-256 of the provider wrapping-key resource identifier and\nis included in every proof. Deployment must policy-bind that proof key and\nwrap/unwrap permission to the same platform principal. The C boundary proves the\nJWT, the pinned-helper proof, and the exact transcript; it cannot prove cloud IAM","doc_id":"8a652d2fcf6d47c854766314","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:15300:{"content":"## Why P5 is split\n\nThe proposal's guarantees are coupled at the point where kb can cause a server\nmutation. A reverse TLS client or JWT verifier is not independently safe if it can\nreach a write before endpoint pinning, next-request revocation, durable replay\nrejection, propagated actor identity, and the authoritative kb WORM intent all exist.\nP5 therefore lands as four ordered, independently security-closed slices. No slice\nbefore P5-C exposes a management write.\n\n1. **P5-A — authoritative registry and role-separated certificate topology.** Build\n   the primary-backed enrollment/heartbeat/lookup substrate and prove two nodes use\n   distinct `clientAuth` and `serverAuth` leaves. The management action route remains\n   fail-closed.\n2. **P5-B — pinned reverse mTLS and nonce-bound revocation status.** Add connect-time\n   address revalidation/IP pinning, enrolled server-certificate pinning, a dedicated\n   status-authority credential, and the server challenge/staple protocol. Enable only\n   a read-only health probe.\n3. **P5-C — operator authorization and audited single-server actions.** Add kb token\n   minting, authenticated generation-bearing JWKS lifecycle, durable server-local\n   `jti` consumption, primary kb WORM intent/outcome, and the real `remote_writes` /\n   capability-gated server action. This is the first slice allowed to mutate.\n4. **P5-D — console/OIDC propagation and fleet UX.** Preserve the composite OIDC or\n   break-glass actor through console→kb, add the server-scoped console allowlist and\n   fleet drill-down, and finish OpenAPI/route coverage. Bulk orchestration remains a\n   later proposal.\n\nP7 supplies custody, key-use admission, anti-rollback building blocks, and the WORM\nledger. P5 owns the revocation-generation schema, online status protocol, management\ntoken/JWKS contract, durable `jti` store, and management audit state machine.","doc_id":"9530c7eabc231f16be186619","doc_kind":""}

Resource-oriented naming\n  (`/v1/enrollments`, `POST /v1/enrollments/{id}/revoke`) rather than verb-suffixing the\n  existing `/v1/enroll/*` bootstrap routes.\n- **`POST /v1/enrollments/{id}/revoke`** — mark revoked. **Two enforcement points** (they are\n  distinct code paths): (a) revoked **cert fingerprints** rejected at the **mTLS handshake /\n  request-auth** layer (`kb_tls_serve.c`), and (b) revoked **bearer scopes** rejected in the\n  scope-authorization path — *not* only \"the verifier seam\", which is OIDC/JWT-only. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:16356:{"content":"## Boundary and rulings\n\nOffline-provision the two independent trust roots required by P5-C2:\n\n1. a fixed RSA-3072 management-token signing key; and\n2. a distinct Ed25519 JWKS-manifest signing root.\n\nPersist only custody-encrypted private material plus exact public bindings. Produce a recoverable public deployment bundle containing the token `kid`/JWK and the manifest verification pin. Bind, but do not advance, the separately configured signed publication-HWM identity that C2b will use to reserve JWKS generations.\n\nThis packet has no JWKS generation/document/signature, online signer, token mint, key-use admission, listener, socket, HTTP route, server cache, rotation, retirement, revocation, overlap, console action, or network dispatch. `/v1/management/action` remains unconditional `503`. Ordinary KB and server targets link none of the new provisioner/private-custody objects. All new private-use paths are reachable only from the offline provisioner.\n\nThe existing status-authority key is never reused. A rotating or compromised token key therefore cannot authorize its own JWKS replacement. The manifest public pin is installed through owner-controlled deployment/enrollment configuration and is never learned from a later JWKS response.\n\nUse fixed RSA-3072, exponent 65537, two-prime PKCS#8 for the token key. This fits the existing 4096-byte protected-use ceiling while the C1a verifier retains its general 2048..8192-bit interoperability. The manifest root is exactly one 32-byte Ed25519 seed. Both use distinct domain-separated AAD, key slots, custody identities, signed HWMs, envelope digests, bootstrap ids, and WORM actions.","doc_id":"9f3c7d1cd534221bde793f87","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:16858:{"content":"## The one fact that determines the whole architecture\n\nThe user runs aimee-server; the organization runs aimee-kb. From the org's point of view aimee-server is therefore an untrusted process — the user controls its memory, its env, its disk. Two consequences follow, and they are not optional:\n\n1. **Org vendor keys must never reach aimee-server.** A key placed in a user-controlled process is a key handed to the user. Therefore aimee-kb — not the server — must be the **egress authority** for org models: server → kb → vendor. The server sees prompts and completions, never an org key.\n2. **Identity is federated, not key-shaped.** Machines/servers always authenticate with enrollment certs (`cert:CN`); when the org configures it on kb, users additionally authenticate with OIDC (the org IdP). aimee-kb therefore always knows who is calling — which is exactly what a \"virtual key\" would otherwise be inventing.\n\n**OIDC is optional — never required unless configured on aimee-kb.** It layers on additively (exactly as the existing verifier does — opt-in via `AIMEE_KB_OIDC_JWKS_FILE`, registered after the owner token). The always-present identity is the enrollment cert; when no OIDC is configured, team binding and attribution key off `cert:CN` and the existing owner-token/bearer auth, and nothing in the series stops working. A single-org box with no IdP still runs the whole plan on certs alone.","doc_id":"a406abe15cd9115658506280","doc_kind":""}

The existing per-request enrollment precheck remains defense in depth, but the new facade is the route's exact registry/enrollment authority. The builder accepts one already-authorized immutable claim tuple and one\nnarrow RS256 signing callback. It validates and canonically serializes the tuple, asks the callback\nto sign only the resulting protected signing input, and returns a compact token in caller-owned\nbounded storage.\n\nThis packet deliberately does not generate or persist `jti`, correlation id, time, `kid`, actor,\nteam, target, peer identity, or request digest. P5-C1c owns their primary-authoritative admission\nand immutable replay tuple; P5-C2 binds the admitted `kid` to a production custody key and supplies\nthe signing callback. Keeping those values explicit makes exact retry deterministic and prevents a\nlater database authority from fighting hidden mint-side randomness or clock reads. No production\nAPI accepts or returns a private PEM or arbitrary key bytes.\n\nThere is no PostgreSQL/schema change, custody/HWM implementation, key provisioning, JWKS\npublication/fetch, network dispatch, listener allowlist change, or route enablement here.\n`/v1/management/action` remains unconditional `503`.","doc_id":"b389844e6d808677d317b650","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:18987:{"content":"## Durable server cache and refresh policy\n\nUse DB1 as the server-local authority so cache bytes and the monotonic generation/HWM commit atomically with the existing FULLMUTEX/WAL transaction gate and backup lifecycle. Add an immutable generation row plus singleton current pointer bound to generation, validity, exact JWKS/payload/envelope bytes and digests, previous/manifest digests, manifest id/public-root digest, trust-bundle digest, and fetch time. A `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction validates current state, inserts only an absent byte-identical generation, and advances the singleton pointer atomically. Commit ambiguity is unavailable; it never authorizes from presumed state. DB1 unavailable, busy, corrupt, inconsistent, or constraint failure denies and clears output.\n\nAt startup, after DB1 initialization and before listener acceptance, validate the configured trust bundle and any cached row. One authenticated refresh is allowed when configured. Consumer authorization uses the exact half-open interval `valid_from <= now && now < valid_until`; it grants no clock-skew extension beyond signed times. A refresh should be scheduled before expiry, but failure may continue using the artifact only until `valid_until`. Startup outage is nonfatal only if the cache is already cryptographically valid and currently in that interval; an empty or stale cache leaves management authorization unavailable and emits a bounded operator warning/availability metric without artifact or token bytes. This slice does not make the server data plane unavailable, and the existing unconditional `/v1/management/action` 503 remains unchanged regardless of cache state.\n\nExpose a cache lookup/refresh orchestrator with a single-flight mutex/condition. A known `kid` uses a currently valid cache without network. An empty cache or a strictly well-formed cache missing an otherwise valid token header `kid` makes exactly one authenticated mTLS fetch; concurrent waiters share that attempt; the verifier retries once and then rejects. A malformed JWKS, token header, signature, or claims is INVALID and never triggers network access. Transient fetch failure never deletes or replaces the last valid cache, but an expired/not-yet-valid cache cannot authorize.","doc_id":"b83d78e2739f210cb6f67d97","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:19731:{"content":"## Canonical wire contract\n\nPublish one canonical bounded UTF-8 JSON envelope whose exact member order is fixed and whose payload is independently canonical. The payload members are: `format_version` (1), `generation` (1), `valid_from` (integer Unix seconds), `valid_until` (integer Unix seconds), `previous_manifest_sha256` (64 zero hex for the first generation), `keys` (an array containing exactly the canonical six-member C2a RSA JWK), and `jwks_sha256` (lowercase SHA-256 of the canonical `{\"keys\":[...]}` JWKS bytes). The outer envelope contains `payload`, `manifest_kid`, `signature_alg` (`EdDSA`), `signature` (canonical unpadded base64url of the 64-byte Ed25519 signature over the exact payload bytes), and `manifest_sha256` (lowercase SHA-256 of a length-framed transcript containing the payload, manifest id, algorithm, and raw signature). No component reserializes a parsed object for signature verification.\n\nTimes are explicit operator inputs accepted only as canonical decimal integers. Require `valid_from` within a small configured clock-skew bound of the offline process clock, `valid_until > valid_from`, and lifetime within a fixed short maximum used later by C2c. They are persisted at STAGED and never recomputed during resume/export. The artifact contains no host, run id, helper path, custody identity, ciphertext, provider attestation, or mutable endpoint.\n\nReuse the exported C2a `kb_mgmt_token_jwk`/public-binding implementation rather than introducing a second encoder, and require C2b's fixture to byte-compare its embedded JWK against C2a's frozen JWK fixture. Freeze byte fixtures for the payload, standalone JWKS object, signature transcript, signature, envelope, and every digest. The standalone canonical `{\"keys\":[...]}` bytes are hashed into `jwks_sha256`; the signed payload embeds the same `keys` array, while the finalized outer envelope is a distinct object. Reject duplicate/unknown members, invalid UTF-8, padding/noncanonical base64url, over-bound arrays/strings, noncanonical RSA encodings, and arithmetic overflow in time validation.","doc_id":"bf69d8e852d8a7cd502fff99","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:20649:{"content":"## Boundary and dependency ruling\n\nAdd the primary-authoritative, tenant-scoped journal for one privileged `remote_writes` action. The journal durably binds authorization, the complete C1b mint tuple, request digest, and both management-certificate identities to one correlation id and JTI before a later packet may create a token or send a network byte. A terminal outcome is appended with a second atomic WORM record.\n\nThe design roundtable retained the accepted order C1c then C2. C1c validates and replay-protects a syntactically valid `kid`, but **does not make that kid or the returned tuple dispatch-eligible**. C2 must bind the exact kid to an admitted active custody key; C3 must obtain it through that authority, recheck the admitted snapshots, mint/sign, and dispatch. No C1c caller can sign or dispatch, and `/v1/management/action` remains unconditional `503`.\n\nUse two immutable append tables rather than a mutable `intent -> dispatching -> terminal` row. A committed intent proves authorization existed, not whether an irreversible remote effect occurred. Intent-only therefore means unresolved and is never automatically redispatched. A definite result appends one outcome; a transport-ambiguous result appends terminal `indeterminate`. Later reconciliation, if required, is a new append-only event in a later packet and never rewrites history.\n\nThis packet has no signing key, private-key API, JWKS, network client, endpoint selection, action handler, automatic recovery worker, or server-side route change.","doc_id":"c7fd7dce6e46732626e122bf","doc_kind":""}

Until that unit lands the registry remains empty/disabled, so the isolated\nauthority core has no reachable live signing path.\n\nP5-B2 owns verified platform workload identity, distinct per-instance management-leaf\nbootstrap/renewal, custodied identity storage, and renewal-expiry repair. P5-B3 owns\nchallenge -> authority -> health orchestration and CT260/CT262. P5-C owns management\nJWT/JWKS/jti and WORM action intent/outcome; P5-D owns human OIDC/console/fleet UX.","doc_id":"d90cb19086ca6b2155bfc56a","doc_kind":""}

It persists unique `jti` + expiry in\nthe server's local database before action, so restart cannot reopen replay. kb writes\na tenant-qualified, correlated WORM intent before network dispatch and an outcome\nafterward; an intent failure prevents dispatch and an ambiguous result stays\nindeterminate. The target server still enforces its own capability and\n`remote_writes` setting.","doc_id":"dd3b5b99d1d748e943c18332","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:22923:{"content":"## What already exists (why this is wiring, not green-field)\n\nThe four-way code survey (2026-07-17) found aimee already owns most of the hard primitives the commercial tools charge enterprise money for:\n\n- **Cost accounting — strong.** Per-request token→USD in the `token_audit` DB1 table (`src/db1/token_audit.c`, `src/server/token_tracker.c`): multi-source pricing (static table → registry/models.dev → authoritative DB1 `model_pricing`), attributed by model/source/role/tool/session/principal/delegation with parent cost-fold. Read surface exists: `GET /v1/insights/overview`, `/v1/dashboard/*`, React `CostPanel`. **Missing only the per-team/project dimension.**\n- **Credential vault — encrypted at rest**, keyed by attested principal (`src/server/vault_service.c`, `src/headers/vault_principal.h`).\n- **OIDC/JWT verifier — real** (RS256/JWKS, alg-pinned), in aimee-kb and kb-console (`src/kb/auth_oidc.c`, `kb-console/auth.go`) — opt-in via env today.\n- **PKI + mTLS enrollment CA** (`src/kb/enroll.c`, `src/kb/pki.c`, `src/server/kb_client_mtls.c`) — `aimee://` single-use tokens, `cert:CN` principals. Reusable for enrolling servers.\n- **Canonical IR + provider drivers** (`src/headers/aimee_ir.h`, `src/server/delegate_driver.c`, `aimee-universal-gateway.md`, done) — Anthropic / OpenAI-Chat / Responses / Gemini wire adapters through a protocol-neutral pivot. This is the egress machinery kb needs.\n- **Keyless roster + attested credential handling already exist** — the shipped `deploy/container/agents.json` ships no keys. The old client-push `POST /v1/session/credentials` was retired; provider secrets now live in the server vault (`/v1/vault/*`), and vault writes require an attested transport (UDS or confidential TLS+bearer — never plaintext TCP; `server_cert.c:18-22`, `server_http_identity.c:113-123`). The org-egress work reuses this attested-transport discipline rather than inventing a new one — org keys simply never leave kb in the first place.\n\nAbsent (the actual gaps, one sub-proposal each): a team/project entity; per-team/project cost attribution; per-team budgets and per-key rate limits (spend is tracked but never capped; the rate limiter is a single global bucket); OIDC on the aimee-server data plane + a kb→server control plane; and AWS Bedrock.","doc_id":"dda697a78df9eb34862d936f","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:24008:{"content":"## Kb runtime ownership and configuration\n\nAdd `src/kb/kb_management_runtime.{h,c}`. The singleton is initialized after DB2 and vault\nstartup synchronization but before `kb_http_start()`, and is stopped after `kb_http_stop()` has\njoined request workers but before DB2/provider teardown. It owns, in destruction order, the\nregistered route callback, B2c lifecycle, B2a provider, copied CA PEM, pins, and public\nverification key. No request may observe a partially initialized or already-closing runtime.\n\nThe singleton has one explicit mutex-protected state machine:\n\n`DISABLED` (the whole packet absent) → `RECONCILING` → `READY`, with `RETRY_WAIT`,\n`READY_DEGRADED`, `TERMINAL`, and `STOPPING` side states. A syntactically configured runtime\nregisters its route callback before HTTP starts, but that callback returns typed `UNAVAILABLE`\nunless state is `READY` or `READY_DEGRADED`; it never treats pending startup as disabled. Static\nconfiguration failure aborts startup before registration. A retryable failure before first\nsuccess enters `RETRY_WAIT`; after at least one successful reconcile it enters\n`READY_DEGRADED`, where B3a still independently rejects an expired or unusable active leaf.\nIntegrity/denied/invalid lifecycle outcomes enter `TERMINAL`, whose callback remains a stable\n503 until restart/operator repair. `STOPPING` rejects new references; HTTP is stopped and joined\nbefore lifecycle/provider memory is cleansed and freed. A borrower that observes `STOPPING`\nreturns `UNAVAILABLE` without dereferencing the lifecycle/provider adapters; unregister blocks\nnew borrows and waits for the in-flight count to reach zero before any owned object destruction.\n\nConfiguration is operator/root supplied through a single explicit environment packet:\n\n- `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_INSTALLATION_ID` (exact 32 lowercase hex),\n  `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_CUSTODIED_CA_DIR`, and `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_BUNDLE_DIR`;\n- `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_WORKLOAD_HELPER`, `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_WORKLOAD_JWKS`,\n  `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_WORKLOAD_PROOF_SPKI`, `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_WORKLOAD_ISSUER`, and","doc_id":"e87a6b20604b71947992cfbc","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:24042:{"content":"## Management-listener protocol\n\nAdd only these routes to the distinct required-mTLS management listener:\n\n- `POST /v1/management/read/challenge` with exact empty body, returning a bounded fresh nonce for\n  purpose `management.read.v1`; and\n- `GET /v1/management/read/agents` with no query or body.\n\nThe agents request carries only the short-lived bearer token and exact nonce-bound signed status\nproof required by B3. The server validates listener/peer EKU and policy, live peer status,\npurpose/nonce/generation/freshness, token signature/kid/generation/audience/cert binding/team/\ncapability/path/digest/expiry, and durably consumes the JTI before rendering. It performs the C3\nprimary checkpoint after authentication and immediately before returning data. Authority/JWKS/\nstatus/checkpoint outage fails closed. Generic data-plane agent/config routes are never registered\non the management listener.\n\nThe challenge is admitted using the base management mTLS chain, dedicated clientAuth EKU/policy,\ncertificate syntax/pin, and local generation/high-water checks. It does not and cannot require the\nfresh nonce-bound proof that it exists to enable. Its exact response is no more than 512 bytes and\ncontains no extra fields:\n`{\"nonce\":\"<43-character unpadded base64url encoding of 32 bytes>\",\"purpose\":\"management.read.v1\",\"expires_at\":<unix-seconds>}`.\nThe nonce has a 15-second lifetime, is bound to that peer/session and one read request, and is\nsingle-use. Receiving it confers no authorization and exposes no fleet data. Entropy failure,\nclock failure, malformed body, replay, expiry, session change, or capacity exhaustion fails closed\nwith the bounded error schema below.\n\nThe server generates the challenge `purpose` from a closed enum containing exactly\n`management.read.v1`; it accepts no caller-supplied purpose. The kb challenge parser requires the\nexact field set and exact purpose before constructing an intent. The signed status proof carries\nthe same closed purpose and the server verifies it byte-for-byte; an unknown or action purpose is","doc_id":"e8d018991452fbedcfba77bc","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:24131:{"content":"## Boundary and rulings\n\nOffline-provision the two independent trust roots required by P5-C2:\n\n1. a fixed RSA-3072 management-token signing key; and\n2. a distinct Ed25519 JWKS-manifest signing root.\n\nPersist only custody-encrypted private material plus exact public bindings. Produce a recoverable public deployment bundle containing the token `kid`/JWK and the manifest verification pin. Bind, but do not advance, the separately configured signed publication-HWM identity that C2b will use to reserve JWKS generations.\n\nThis packet has no JWKS generation/document/signature, online signer, token mint, key-use admission, listener, socket, HTTP route, server cache, rotation, retirement, revocation, overlap, console action, or network dispatch. `/v1/management/action` remains unconditional `503`. Ordinary KB and server targets link none of the new provisioner/private-custody objects. All new private-use paths are reachable only from the offline provisioner.\n\nThe existing status-authority key is never reused. A rotating or compromised token key therefore cannot authorize its own JWKS replacement. The manifest public pin is installed through owner-controlled deployment/enrollment configuration and is never learned from a later JWKS response.\n\nUse fixed RSA-3072, exponent 65537, two-prime PKCS#8 for the token key. This fits the existing 4096-byte protected-use ceiling while the C1a verifier retains its general 2048..8192-bit interoperability. The manifest root is exactly one 32-byte Ed25519 seed. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:24313:{"content":"## Kb runtime ownership and configuration\n\nAdd `src/kb/kb_management_runtime.{h,c}`. The singleton is initialized after DB2 and vault\nstartup synchronization but before `kb_http_start()`, and is stopped after `kb_http_stop()` has\njoined request workers but before DB2/provider teardown. It owns, in destruction order, the\nregistered route callback, B2c lifecycle, B2a provider, copied CA PEM, pins, and public\nverification key. No request may observe a partially initialized or already-closing runtime.\n\nThe singleton has one explicit mutex-protected state machine:\n\n`DISABLED` (the whole packet absent) → `RECONCILING` → `READY`, with `RETRY_WAIT`,\n`READY_DEGRADED`, `TERMINAL`, and `STOPPING` side states. A syntactically configured runtime\nregisters its route callback before HTTP starts, but that callback returns typed `UNAVAILABLE`\nunless state is `READY` or `READY_DEGRADED`; it never treats pending startup as disabled. Static\nconfiguration failure aborts startup before registration. A retryable failure before first\nsuccess enters `RETRY_WAIT`; after at least one successful reconcile it enters\n`READY_DEGRADED`, where B3a still independently rejects an expired or unusable active leaf.\nIntegrity/denied/invalid lifecycle outcomes enter `TERMINAL`, whose callback remains a stable\n503 until restart/operator repair. `STOPPING` rejects new references; HTTP is stopped and joined\nbefore lifecycle/provider memory is cleansed and freed. A borrower that observes `STOPPING`\nreturns `UNAVAILABLE` without dereferencing the lifecycle/provider adapters; unregister blocks\nnew borrows and waits for the in-flight count to reach zero before any owned object destruction.\n\nConfiguration is operator/root supplied through a single explicit environment packet:\n\n- `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_INSTALLATION_ID` (exact 32 lowercase hex),\n  `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_CUSTODIED_CA_DIR`, and `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_BUNDLE_DIR`;\n- `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_WORKLOAD_HELPER`, `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_WORKLOAD_JWKS`,\n  `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_WORKLOAD_PROOF_SPKI`, `AIMEE_KB_MGMT_WORKLOAD_ISSUER`, and","doc_id":"eb61bd1556964d84d03ba79d","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:24486:{"content":"## KB runtime adapter\n\nAdd a small runtime-only DB2 adapter that calls the new facade on the primary connection and accepts exactly one row followed by DONE. It bounds generation, candidate id, validity, envelope length, and every digest; rejects embedded NUL; recomputes the envelope SHA-256; and clears all output on failure. It does not link any offline JWKS publisher, root provisioner, vault recovery, manifest signer, or HWM provider object.\n\nThe mTLS listener passes only its TLS-derived triple to this adapter. The existing per-request enrollment precheck remains defense in depth, but the new facade is the route's exact registry/enrollment authority. Both checks must allow: the precheck may fail fast before the facade, while a precheck allow never overrides a facade denial. An authenticated leaf that passes the broad issuer/serial precheck but fails exact registry/fingerprint/purpose/expiry binding is 403. Tests force disagreement in both directions and prove no route success unless the intersection allows.","doc_id":"ed0c9966c8254e7c7f579e6d","doc_kind":""}

A compromised console is bounded to that allowlist. It may\n  mint client enrollments, but the kb **refuses to mint an owner or privileged\n  scope for a console-admin caller**: the requested scope must be a proper\n  `<kind>:<id>` and the kind may not be `owner`/`console-admin`/`curator`, so the\n  console cannot escalate by minting. `/v1/review` is **not** in the set: review\n  accept/reject is a separate `curator` scope. (The console is on the kb's compose\n  network, so other services on it can reach the console port, but every action\n  still requires a valid console session: OIDC or break-glass.)\n- **Deny-by-default proxy.** `/api/*` maps 1:1 to the allowlisted `/v1` routes and\n  re-checks the same allowlist in Go (`acl.go`) before forwarding, defence in\n  depth with the kb's server-side check. The browser's own token is never\n  forwarded; only the console-admin bearer, server-side.\n- **Login = OIDC primary.** The console verifies a browser-presented OIDC JWT\n  itself (RS256 only, `iss`/`aud`/`exp`/`nbf` checked, JWKS by `kid`) and requires\n  a pinned admin claim. This is a port of `src/kb/auth_oidc.c`; a parity test\n  locks the claim mapping.\n- **Break-glass is off by default.** A static console-admin bearer login is\n  enabled only when the operator drops a presence-flag file\n  (`$KB_CONSOLE_HOME/.break_glass`, mode 0600). Break-glass sessions are capped at\n  **300 s** and audited (console-local record now; a kb-side `audit_events` row is\n  added with the auth endpoints in S2a). /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-19t18bi3/large-repo-c0ef1874783e461f/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:25842:{"content":"## Why P5 is split\n\nThe proposal's guarantees are coupled at the point where kb can cause a server\nmutation. A reverse TLS client or JWT verifier is not independently safe if it can\nreach a write before endpoint pinning, next-request revocation, durable replay\nrejection, propagated actor identity, and the authoritative kb WORM intent all exist.\nP5 therefore lands as four ordered, independently security-closed slices. No slice\nbefore P5-C exposes a management write.\n\n1. **P5-A — authoritative registry and role-separated certificate topology.** Build\n   the primary-backed enrollment/heartbeat/lookup substrate and prove two nodes use\n   distinct `clientAuth` and `serverAuth` leaves. The management action route remains\n   fail-closed.\n2. **P5-B — pinned reverse mTLS and nonce-bound revocation status.** Add connect-time\n   address revalidation/IP pinning, enrolled server-certificate pinning, a dedicated\n   status-authority credential, and the server challenge/staple protocol.
